host.note: Reconstructed session: the replies were written by an agent playing this session; every embed was computed by the host from the graphs named. The building is the Schependomlaan design model (CC BY 4.0, (C) original owners), converted to BIM Open Schema tables; NOTICE.md has the attribution.

request.text: Open schependomlaan.duckdb. What storeys does it have?

reply.text: Six storeys, from `-1 fundering` (foundation) at -1000 up to `04 dak` (roof) at 12000, 3000 apart. The file records no unit for these values; the 3000 spacing reads as millimetres. The four floors with rooms, `00 begane grond` (ground floor) to `03 derde verdieping` (third floor), carry a gross floor area between 195.9 and 339.6; the foundation and the roof carry 0.

embeds.caption: Storeys with elevation, height, and gross floor area as the file gives them

request.text: How many spaces per storey? Chart it.

reply.text: 100 spaces, all on the four middle storeys: 32 on the ground floor, 29 on the first, 20 on the second, 19 on the third. The foundation and roof storeys have none. The graph filters `EntityText` to IFCSPACE, joins `StoreyOfElement` for the storey, and counts per storey.
205 doors and 259 windows. The ground floor has the most doors (80), the first floor the most windows (88). The roof storey has 5 windows and no doors; the foundation has neither.

request.text: Show me the building, coloured by IFC class.

reply.text: The 3D view loads `schependomlaan.bos` and colours each element placed on a storey by its class: 3,621 elements in 11 named colours plus grey for the 109 in smaller classes. Spaces are left out so they do not hide the walls; the query also drops entities with no STEP id (StepId -1), which the 3D view cannot match, though none of them sits on a storey.Coverings (1,262) and walls (652, plus 282 standard-case walls) are most of it. The table is the legend's counts.
